item.title: A Hotel Had Already Put the Family on Its “Do Not Rent” List
item.description: Five-year-old Xaquie Bynum died from carbon monoxide poisoning inside her New Mexico home. A lawsuit now claims child welfare officials had received repeated reports about the family and had even warned them about unsafe heating methods. Could her death have been prevented?

item.title: His Hair Was Found Inside Emma’s Burned-Out Car
item.description: Twenty-year-old Emma Agnew disappeared after arranging to meet someone interested in buying her car. Her burned-out vehicle was later found, and the investigation led to Liam Reid. Just nine days later, another young woman survived an attack that would become crucial to the case.

item.title: She Was NOT in the Mood for Questions
item.description: A welfare check at the Fort Smith home of 72-year-old retired teacher William “Bill” DuBois Jr. quickly became a murder investigation. When police tracked his missing car, the trail led to Taylor Elkins — a former student who would eventually be convicted of his murder and sentenced to 40 years in prison.
